import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 4.56

by K. W. Roggenkamp

Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring with $1$, and $\Lambda$ an $R$-algebra which is
finitely generated as an $R$-module. Put
$$T = \{U \in \mathrm{Mod}\,\Lambda \mid \exists \text{ an exact } \Lambda\text{-sequence }
0 \to P \to \Lambda^{(n)} \to U \to 0 \text{ for some } n, \text{ with }
P_m \cong \Lambda_m^{(n)} \text{ for every maximal ideal } m \text{ of } R\}.$$
Denote by $\mathbb{G}(T)$ the Grothendieck group of $T$ relative to short exact sequences.

a) Describe $\mathbb{G}(T)$, in particular, what does it mean: $[U] = [V]$ in $\mathbb{G}(T)$?

b) *Conjecture:* if $\dim(\max(R)) = d < \infty$, and there are two epimorphisms
$\varphi \colon \Lambda^{(n)} \to U$, $\psi \colon \Lambda^{(n)} \to V$, $n > d$, and
$[U] = [V]$ in $\mathbb{G}(T)$, then $\operatorname{Ker} \varphi = \operatorname{Ker} \psi$.

Only part b) is a statement; part a) asks for a description and is not formalized.

Here $\Lambda$ is a possibly noncommutative $R$-algebra and $\mathrm{Mod}\,\Lambda$ consists of
left $\Lambda$-modules. $P_m$ and $\Lambda_m$ denote the localizations at the maximal ideal $m$
of $R$, i.e. the (Ore) localizations at the central image of $R \setminus m$ in $\Lambda$, and
$P_m \cong \Lambda_m^{(n)}$ is an isomorphism of $\Lambda_m$-modules. The equality
$\operatorname{Ker} \varphi = \operatorname{Ker} \psi$ is read as an isomorphism of
$\Lambda$-modules: literal equality of submodules of $\Lambda^{(n)}$ fails trivially after
precomposing $\varphi$ with an automorphism of $\Lambda^{(n)}$, so the conjecture is a
cancellation statement in the style of Bass. $\dim(\max(R))$ is the Krull dimension of the
maximal spectrum of $R$ with its Zariski topology. The modules $U$ in $T$ are quotients of
$\Lambda^{(n)}$, hence finitely generated left $\Lambda$-modules.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/
open scoped OreLocalization
namespace Kourovka.«4.56»
universe u v

instance oreSet_algebraMapSubmonoid (S : Submonoid R) :
    OreLocalization.OreSet (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid Λ S) where
  ore_right_cancel r₁ r₂ s h := by
    obtain ⟨x, -, hx⟩ := s.2
    refine ⟨s, ?_⟩
    rw [← hx, Algebra.commutes, Algebra.commutes, hx]
    exact h
  oreNum r _ := r
  oreDenom _ s := s
  ore_eq r s := by
    obtain ⟨x, -, hx⟩ := s.2
    rw [← hx, Algebra.commutes]
blocks.docstring:
The image in `Λ` of a submonoid `S` of the commutative base ring `R` is a (left) Ore set,
because its elements are central in `Λ`. This makes the localizations `Λ[S⁻¹]` and `P[S⁻¹]`
of `Λ` and of a `Λ`-module `P` available as a ring and a module over it.

justification.closest_existing_considered: OreLocalization.oreSetComm (commutative case only); LocalizedModule S M (no Module structure over the localized noncommutative algebra); TensorProduct.Algebra.module (not an instance, no right-factor Λ action on A ⊗[R] P).
justification.name: Kourovka.«4.56».oreSet_algebraMapSubmonoid
justification.why_needed: Mathlib only has `OreSet` instances for submonoids of commutative monoids and for ⊥; localizing the (noncommutative) R-algebra Λ and its modules at the central multiplicative set image of R∖m requires an `OreSet` instance for `Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid Λ M`.

  Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid Λ m.asIdeal.primeCompl

variable (Λ) in

def IsLocallyFreeOfRankAt (m : MaximalSpectrum R) (P : Type*) [AddCommGroup P] [Module Λ P]
    (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  Nonempty (P[(primeComplIn Λ m)⁻¹] ≃ₗ[Λ[(primeComplIn Λ m)⁻¹]]
    (Fin n → Λ[(primeComplIn Λ m)⁻¹]))
blocks.docstring:
The condition $P_m \cong \Lambda_m^{(n)}$: the localization $P_m$ of the `Λ`-module `P` at
the maximal ideal `m` of `R` is isomorphic, as a module over the localization $\Lambda_m$, to
the free module $\Lambda_m^{(n)}$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Module.rankAtStalk`, `Module.Free (Localization.AtPrime m) _`, `Module.FinitePresentation`-style locally-free predicates — all for modules over commutative rings only.
justification.name: Kourovka.«4.56».IsLocallyFreeOfRankAt
justification.why_needed: Expresses `P_m ≅ Λ_m^{(n)}` as a Λ_m-linear isomorphism `P[S⁻¹] ≃ₗ[Λ[S⁻¹]] (Fin n → Λ[S⁻¹])`; Mathlib has no notion of local freeness of a module over a noncommutative algebra at a maximal ideal of the base ring.

blocks.name: IsLocallyFreeOfRankAt
blocks.text:
variable (Λ) in
/-- The condition $P_m \cong \Lambda_m^{(n)}$: the localization $P_m$ of the `Λ`-module `P` at
the maximal ideal `m` of `R` is isomorphic, as a module over the localization $\Lambda_m$, to
the free module $\Lambda_m^{(n)}$. -/
def IsLocallyFreeOfRankAt (m : MaximalSpectrum R) (P : Type*) [AddCommGroup P] [Module Λ P]
    (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  Nonempty (P[(primeComplIn Λ m)⁻¹] ≃ₗ[Λ[(primeComplIn Λ m)⁻¹]]
    (Fin n → Λ[(primeComplIn Λ m)⁻¹]))

blocks.docstring:
The class `T`: a `Λ`-module `U` belongs to `T` if there is an exact sequence of
`Λ`-modules $0 \to P \to \Lambda^{(n)} \to U \to 0$ for some $n$ with
$P_m \cong \Lambda_m^{(n)}$ for every maximal ideal $m$ of $R$. The module `P` is taken to be
the kernel of the epimorphism $\Lambda^{(n)} \to U$, to which it is isomorphic.

justification.closest_existing_considered: No Mathlib counterpart; `Module.Projective`, `Module.Free` do not capture the rank-n local freeness of the kernel.
justification.name: Kourovka.«4.56».MemT
justification.why_needed: Membership in the class T of the problem: existence of a surjection φ : Λ^(n) → U whose kernel is locally free of rank n at every maximal ideal of R.

blocks.name: MemT
blocks.text:
variable (R Λ) in
/-- The class `T`: a `Λ`-module `U` belongs to `T` if there is an exact sequence of
`Λ`-modules $0 \to P \to \Lambda^{(n)} \to U \to 0$ for some $n$ with
$P_m \cong \Lambda_m^{(n)}$ for every maximal ideal $m$ of $R$. The module `P` is taken to be
the kernel of the epimorphism $\Lambda^{(n)} \to U$, to which it is isomorphic. -/
def MemT (U : Type*) [AddCommGroup U] [Module Λ U] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (φ : (Fin n → Λ) →ₗ[Λ] U), Function.Surjective φ ∧
    ∀ m : MaximalSpectrum R, IsLocallyFreeOfRankAt Λ m (LinearMap.ker φ) n

blocks.code: def TObj : Type (v + 1) := {U : ModuleCat.{v} Λ // MemT R Λ U}
blocks.docstring:
The `Λ`-modules in the class `T`, bundled. Every module in `T` is a quotient of
`Fin n → Λ`, so it is isomorphic to one in the universe of `Λ`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `ModuleCat Λ` (used as the carrier), `CategoryTheory.FullSubcategory` (unnecessary categorical overhead).
justification.name: Kourovka.«4.56».TObj
justification.why_needed: Bundled Λ-modules in T (`{U : ModuleCat.{v} Λ // MemT R Λ U}`), the generating set of the free abelian group.

blocks.name: TObj
blocks.text:
variable (R Λ) in
/-- The `Λ`-modules in the class `T`, bundled. Every module in `T` is a quotient of
`Fin n → Λ`, so it is isomorphic to one in the universe of `Λ`. -/
def TObj : Type (v + 1) := {U : ModuleCat.{v} Λ // MemT R Λ U}

blocks.docstring: A short exact sequence $0 \to A \to B \to C \to 0$ of `Λ`-modules in `T`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.ShortExact` in `ModuleCat Λ` (heavier; `Function.Exact` with injectivity/surjectivity is equivalent and elementary).
justification.name: Kourovka.«4.56».IsShortExact
justification.why_needed: Short exact sequences 0 → A → B → C → 0 of Λ-modules with all terms in T, needed for the Grothendieck relations.

blocks.name: IsShortExact
blocks.text:
/-- A short exact sequence $0 \to A \to B \to C \to 0$ of `Λ`-modules in `T`. -/
def IsShortExact (A B C : TObj R Λ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (f : A.1 →ₗ[Λ] B.1) (g : B.1 →ₗ[Λ] C.1),
    Function.Injective f ∧ Function.Exact f g ∧ Function.Surjective g

blocks.code:
def grothendieckRelations : AddSubgroup (FreeAbelianGroup (TObj R Λ)) :=
  AddSubgroup.closure
    ({x | ∃ A B : TObj R Λ, Nonempty (A.1 ≃ₗ[Λ] B.1) ∧
        x = FreeAbelianGroup.of A - FreeAbelianGroup.of B} ∪
      {x | ∃ A B C : TObj R Λ, IsShortExact A B C ∧
        x = FreeAbelianGroup.of B - (FreeAbelianGroup.of A + FreeAbelianGroup.of C)})
blocks.docstring:
The relations defining the Grothendieck group of `T`: isomorphic modules are identified,
and $[B] = [A] + [C]$ for every short exact sequence $0 \to A \to B \to C \to 0$ in `T`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: None in Mathlib; `Localization.GrothendieckGroup`/`Monoid` group completion is not the K₀ of a class of modules with exact sequences.
justification.name: Kourovka.«4.56».grothendieckRelations
justification.why_needed: The subgroup of the free abelian group on TObj generated by the isomorphism relations and by [B] − ([A] + [C]) for short exact sequences in T.

blocks.name: grothendieckRelations
blocks.text:
variable (R Λ) in
/-- The relations defining the Grothendieck group of `T`: isomorphic modules are identified,
and $[B] = [A] + [C]$ for every short exact sequence $0 \to A \to B \to C \to 0$ in `T`. -/
def grothendieckRelations : AddSubgroup (FreeAbelianGroup (TObj R Λ)) :=
  AddSubgroup.closure
    ({x | ∃ A B : TObj R Λ, Nonempty (A.1 ≃ₗ[Λ] B.1) ∧
        x = FreeAbelianGroup.of A - FreeAbelianGroup.of B} ∪
      {x | ∃ A B C : TObj R Λ, IsShortExact A B C ∧
        x = FreeAbelianGroup.of B - (FreeAbelianGroup.of A + FreeAbelianGroup.of C)})

blocks.code:
abbrev GrothendieckGroup : Type (v + 1) :=
  FreeAbelianGroup (TObj R Λ) ⧸ grothendieckRelations R Λ
blocks.docstring:
The Grothendieck group $\mathbb{G}(T)$ of `T` relative to short exact sequences: the free
abelian group on the (isomorphism classes of) modules in `T`, modulo the relations
$[B] = [A] + [C]$ for the short exact sequences $0 \to A \to B \to C \to 0$ in `T`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: No Grothendieck group / K₀ of a module category or exact category exists in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib.
justification.name: Kourovka.«4.56».GrothendieckGroup
justification.why_needed: The Grothendieck group 𝔾(T) of T relative to short exact sequences, as a quotient of the free abelian group on TObj.

blocks.name: GrothendieckGroup
blocks.text:
variable (R Λ) in
/-- The Grothendieck group $\mathbb{G}(T)$ of `T` relative to short exact sequences: the free
abelian group on the (isomorphism classes of) modules in `T`, modulo the relations
$[B] = [A] + [C]$ for the short exact sequences $0 \to A \to B \to C \to 0$ in `T`. -/
abbrev GrothendieckGroup : Type (v + 1) :=
  FreeAbelianGroup (TObj R Λ) ⧸ grothendieckRelations R Λ

blocks.docstring: The class $[U] \in \mathbb{G}(T)$ of a module `U` in `T`.

justification.name: Kourovka.«4.56».grothendieckClass
justification.why_needed: The class [U] ∈ 𝔾(T) of a module U in T, needed to state [U] = [V].

blocks.name: grothendieckClass
blocks.text:
variable (R Λ) in
/-- The class $[U] \in \mathbb{G}(T)$ of a module `U` in `T`. -/
def grothendieckClass (U : Type v) [AddCommGroup U] [Module Λ U] (hU : MemT R Λ U) :
    GrothendieckGroup R Λ :=
  QuotientAddGroup.mk (FreeAbelianGroup.of (⟨ModuleCat.of Λ U, hU⟩ : TObj R Λ))

@[category test, AMS 16 19]
theorem memT_punit : MemT R Λ PUnit := by
  refine ⟨0, 0, fun _ => ⟨0, Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩, fun m => ⟨?_⟩⟩
  haveI : Subsingleton
      (OreLocalization (primeComplIn Λ m) (LinearMap.ker (0 : (Fin 0 → Λ) →ₗ[Λ] PUnit))) := by
    refine ⟨fun x y => ?_⟩
    induction x using OreLocalization.ind with | _ x s => ?_
    induction y using OreLocalization.ind with | _ y t => ?_
    rw [Subsingleton.elim x 0, Subsingleton.elim y 0, OreLocalization.zero_oreDiv,
      OreLocalization.zero_oreDiv]
  exact LinearEquiv.ofSubsingleton _ _

    induction y using OreLocalization.ind with | _ y t => ?_

@[category API, AMS 16 19]
theorem grothendieckClass_eq_of_linearEquiv {U V : Type v} [AddCommGroup U] [Module Λ U]
    [AddCommGroup V] [Module Λ V] (hU : MemT R Λ U) (hV : MemT R Λ V) (e : U ≃ₗ[Λ] V) :
    grothendieckClass R Λ U hU = grothendieckClass R Λ V hV := by
  refine (QuotientAddGroup.eq).mpr (AddSubgroup.subset_closure (Or.inl ?_))
  exact ⟨⟨ModuleCat.of Λ V, hV⟩, ⟨ModuleCat.of Λ U, hU⟩, ⟨e.symm⟩,
    by rw [neg_add_eq_sub]⟩
blocks.docstring: Isomorphic modules in `T` have the same class in $\mathbb{G}(T)$.
blocks.name: grothendieckClass_eq_of_linearEquiv
blocks.text:
/-- Isomorphic modules in `T` have the same class in $\mathbb{G}(T)$. -/
@[category API, AMS 16 19]
theorem grothendieckClass_eq_of_linearEquiv {U V : Type v} [AddCommGroup U] [Module Λ U]
    [AddCommGroup V] [Module Λ V] (hU : MemT R Λ U) (hV : MemT R Λ V) (e : U ≃ₗ[Λ] V) :
    grothendieckClass R Λ U hU = grothendieckClass R Λ V hV := by
  refine (QuotientAddGroup.eq).mpr (AddSubgroup.subset_closure (Or.inl ?_))
  exact ⟨⟨ModuleCat.of Λ V, hV⟩, ⟨ModuleCat.of Λ U, hU⟩, ⟨e.symm⟩,
    by rw [neg_add_eq_sub]⟩

@[category API, AMS 16 19]
theorem grothendieckClass_eq_add_of_shortExact {A B C : Type v}
    [AddCommGroup A] [Module Λ A] [AddCommGroup B] [Module Λ B] [AddCommGroup C] [Module Λ C]
    (hA : MemT R Λ A) (hB : MemT R Λ B) (hC : MemT R Λ C)
    (f : A →ₗ[Λ] B) (g : B →ₗ[Λ] C)
    (hf : Function.Injective f) (hfg : Function.Exact f g) (hg : Function.Surjective g) :
    grothendieckClass R Λ B hB = grothendieckClass R Λ A hA + grothendieckClass R Λ C hC := by
  refine (QuotientAddGroup.eq).mpr ?_
  rw [neg_add_eq_sub, ← neg_sub]
  exact AddSubgroup.neg_mem _ (AddSubgroup.subset_closure (Or.inr ⟨⟨ModuleCat.of Λ A, hA⟩,
    ⟨ModuleCat.of Λ B, hB⟩, ⟨ModuleCat.of Λ C, hC⟩, ⟨f, g, hf, hfg, hg⟩, rfl⟩))
blocks.docstring:
The relation $[B] = [A] + [C]$ in $\mathbb{G}(T)$ for a short exact sequence
$0 \to A \to B \to C \to 0$ in `T`.
blocks.name: grothendieckClass_eq_add_of_shortExact

$0 \to A \to B \to C \to 0$ in `T`. -/
@[category API, AMS 16 19]
theorem grothendieckClass_eq_add_of_shortExact {A B C : Type v}
    [AddCommGroup A] [Module Λ A] [AddCommGroup B] [Module Λ B] [AddCommGroup C] [Module Λ C]
    (hA : MemT R Λ A) (hB : MemT R Λ B) (hC : MemT R Λ C)
    (f : A →ₗ[Λ] B) (g : B →ₗ[Λ] C)
    (hf : Function.Injective f) (hfg : Function.Exact f g) (hg : Function.Surjective g) :
    grothendieckClass R Λ B hB = grothendieckClass R Λ A hA + grothendieckClass R Λ C hC := by
  refine (QuotientAddGroup.eq).mpr ?_
  rw [neg_add_eq_sub, ← neg_sub]
  exact AddSubgroup.neg_mem _ (AddSubgroup.subset_closure (Or.inr ⟨⟨ModuleCat.of Λ A, hA⟩,
    ⟨ModuleCat.of Λ B, hB⟩, ⟨ModuleCat.of Λ C, hC⟩, ⟨f, g, hf, hfg, hg⟩, rfl⟩))

@[category research open, AMS 13 16 19]
theorem kourovka.«4.56».parts.b
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [Module.Finite R Λ]
    {d : ℕ} (hd : topologicalKrullDim (MaximalSpectrum R) = d)
    {U V : Type v} [AddCommGroup U] [Module Λ U] [AddCommGroup V] [Module Λ V]
    (hU : MemT R Λ U) (hV : MemT R Λ V)
    {n : ℕ} (hn : d < n)
    (φ : (Fin n → Λ) →ₗ[Λ] U) (ψ : (Fin n → Λ) →ₗ[Λ] V)
    (hφ : Function.Surjective φ) (hψ : Function.Surjective ψ)
    (hUV : grothendieckClass R Λ U hU = grothendieckClass R Λ V hV) :
    Nonempty (LinearMap.ker φ ≃ₗ[Λ] LinearMap.ker ψ) := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Conjecture (Roggenkamp, Kourovka 4.56 b).** Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring with
$1$ and $\Lambda$ an $R$-algebra which is finitely generated as an $R$-module. Let $T$ be the
class of `Λ`-modules $U$ admitting an exact sequence $0 \to P \to \Lambda^{(n)} \to U \to 0$
with $P_m \cong \Lambda_m^{(n)}$ for every maximal ideal $m$ of $R$, and let $\mathbb{G}(T)$
be the Grothendieck group of $T$ relative to short exact sequences.

If $\dim(\max(R)) = d < \infty$ and there are two epimorphisms
$\varphi \colon \Lambda^{(n)} \to U$, $\psi \colon \Lambda^{(n)} \to V$ with $n > d$ and
$[U] = [V]$ in $\mathbb{G}(T)$, then $\operatorname{Ker} \varphi \cong \operatorname{Ker} \psi$
as $\Lambda$-modules.

Here $\dim(\max(R))$ is the Krull dimension of the maximal spectrum of $R$ with the Zariski
topology, and $U, V \in T$ so that their classes in $\mathbb{G}(T)$ are defined.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 4.56

by K. W. Roggenkamp

Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring with $1$, and $\Lambda$ an $R$-algebra which is
finitely generated as an $R$-module. Put
$$T = \{U \in \mathrm{Mod}\,\Lambda \mid \exists \text{ an exact } \Lambda\text{-sequence }
0 \to P \to \Lambda^{(n)} \to U \to 0 \text{ for some } n, \text{ with }
P_m \cong \Lambda_m^{(n)} \text{ for every maximal ideal } m \text{ of } R\}.$$
Denote by $\mathbb{G}(T)$ the Grothendieck group of $T$ relative to short exact sequences.

a) Describe $\mathbb{G}(T)$, in particular, what does it mean: $[U] = [V]$ in $\mathbb{G}(T)$?

b) *Conjecture:* if $\dim(\max(R)) = d < \infty$, and there are two epimorphisms
$\varphi \colon \Lambda^{(n)} \to U$, $\psi \colon \Lambda^{(n)} \to V$, $n > d$, and
$[U] = [V]$ in $\mathbb{G}(T)$, then $\operatorname{Ker} \varphi = \operatorname{Ker} \psi$.

Only part b) is a statement; part a) asks for a description and is not formalized.

Here $\Lambda$ is a possibly noncommutative $R$-algebra and $\mathrm{Mod}\,\Lambda$ consists of
left $\Lambda$-modules. $P_m$ and $\Lambda_m$ denote the localizations at the maximal ideal $m$
of $R$, i.e. the (Ore) localizations at the central image of $R \setminus m$ in $\Lambda$, and
$P_m \cong \Lambda_m^{(n)}$ is an isomorphism of $\Lambda_m$-modules. The equality
$\operatorname{Ker} \varphi = \operatorname{Ker} \psi$ is read as an isomorphism of
$\Lambda$-modules: literal equality of submodules of $\Lambda^{(n)}$ fails trivially after
precomposing $\varphi$ with an automorphism of $\Lambda^{(n)}$, so the conjecture is a
cancellation statement in the style of Bass. $\dim(\max(R))$ is the Krull dimension of the
maximal spectrum of $R$ with its Zariski topology. The modules $U$ in $T$ are quotients of
$\Lambda^{(n)}$, hence finitely generated left $\Lambda$-modules.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open scoped OreLocalization

namespace Kourovka.«4.56»

universe u v

variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {Λ : Type v} [Ring Λ] [Algebra R Λ]

/-- The image in `Λ` of a submonoid `S` of the commutative base ring `R` is a (left) Ore set,
because its elements are central in `Λ`. This makes the localizations `Λ[S⁻¹]` and `P[S⁻¹]`
of `Λ` and of a `Λ`-module `P` available as a ring and a module over it. -/
instance oreSet_algebraMapSubmonoid (S : Submonoid R) :
    OreLocalization.OreSet (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid Λ S) where
  ore_right_cancel r₁ r₂ s h := by
    obtain ⟨x, -, hx⟩ := s.2
    refine ⟨s, ?_⟩
    rw [← hx, Algebra.commutes, Algebra.commutes, hx]
    exact h
  oreNum r _ := r
  oreDenom _ s := s
  ore_eq r s := by
    obtain ⟨x, -, hx⟩ := s.2
    rw [← hx, Algebra.commutes]

variable (Λ) in
/-- The multiplicative set `R ∖ m`, viewed inside `Λ`, for a maximal ideal `m` of `R`. -/
abbrev primeComplIn (m : MaximalSpectrum R) : Submonoid Λ :=
  Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid Λ m.asIdeal.primeCompl

variable (Λ) in
/-- The condition $P_m \cong \Lambda_m^{(n)}$: the localization $P_m$ of the `Λ`-module `P` at
the maximal ideal `m` of `R` is isomorphic, as a module over the localization $\Lambda_m$, to
the free module $\Lambda_m^{(n)}$. -/
def IsLocallyFreeOfRankAt (m : MaximalSpectrum R) (P : Type*) [AddCommGroup P] [Module Λ P]
    (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  Nonempty (P[(primeComplIn Λ m)⁻¹] ≃ₗ[Λ[(primeComplIn Λ m)⁻¹]]
    (Fin n → Λ[(primeComplIn Λ m)⁻¹]))

variable (R Λ) in
/-- The class `T`: a `Λ`-module `U` belongs to `T` if there is an exact sequence of
`Λ`-modules $0 \to P \to \Lambda^{(n)} \to U \to 0$ for some $n$ with
$P_m \cong \Lambda_m^{(n)}$ for every maximal ideal $m$ of $R$. The module `P` is taken to be
the kernel of the epimorphism $\Lambda^{(n)} \to U$, to which it is isomorphic. -/
def MemT (U : Type*) [AddCommGroup U] [Module Λ U] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (φ : (Fin n → Λ) →ₗ[Λ] U), Function.Surjective φ ∧
    ∀ m : MaximalSpectrum R, IsLocallyFreeOfRankAt Λ m (LinearMap.ker φ) n

variable (R Λ) in
/-- The `Λ`-modules in the class `T`, bundled. Every module in `T` is a quotient of
`Fin n → Λ`, so it is isomorphic to one in the universe of `Λ`. -/
def TObj : Type (v + 1) := {U : ModuleCat.{v} Λ // MemT R Λ U}

/-- A short exact sequence $0 \to A \to B \to C \to 0$ of `Λ`-modules in `T`. -/
def IsShortExact (A B C : TObj R Λ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (f : A.1 →ₗ[Λ] B.1) (g : B.1 →ₗ[Λ] C.1),
    Function.Injective f ∧ Function.Exact f g ∧ Function.Surjective g

variable (R Λ) in
/-- The relations defining the Grothendieck group of `T`: isomorphic modules are identified,
and $[B] = [A] + [C]$ for every short exact sequence $0 \to A \to B \to C \to 0$ in `T`. -/
def grothendieckRelations : AddSubgroup (FreeAbelianGroup (TObj R Λ)) :=
  AddSubgroup.closure
    ({x | ∃ A B : TObj R Λ, Nonempty (A.1 ≃ₗ[Λ] B.1) ∧
        x = FreeAbelianGroup.of A - FreeAbelianGroup.of B} ∪
      {x | ∃ A B C : TObj R Λ, IsShortExact A B C ∧
        x = FreeAbelianGroup.of B - (FreeAbelianGroup.of A + FreeAbelianGroup.of C)})

variable (R Λ) in
/-- The Grothendieck group $\mathbb{G}(T)$ of `T` relative to short exact sequences: the free
abelian group on the (isomorphism classes of) modules in `T`, modulo the relations
$[B] = [A] + [C]$ for the short exact sequences $0 \to A \to B \to C \to 0$ in `T`. -/
abbrev GrothendieckGroup : Type (v + 1) :=
  FreeAbelianGroup (TObj R Λ) ⧸ grothendieckRelations R Λ

variable (R Λ) in
/-- The class $[U] \in \mathbb{G}(T)$ of a module `U` in `T`. -/
def grothendieckClass (U : Type v) [AddCommGroup U] [Module Λ U] (hU : MemT R Λ U) :
    GrothendieckGroup R Λ :=
  QuotientAddGroup.mk (FreeAbelianGroup.of (⟨ModuleCat.of Λ U, hU⟩ : TObj R Λ))

/-- The zero module lies in `T` (take $n = 0$). -/
@[category test, AMS 16 19]
theorem memT_punit : MemT R Λ PUnit := by
  refine ⟨0, 0, fun _ => ⟨0, Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩, fun m => ⟨?_⟩⟩
  haveI : Subsingleton
      (OreLocalization (primeComplIn Λ m) (LinearMap.ker (0 : (Fin 0 → Λ) →ₗ[Λ] PUnit))) := by
    refine ⟨fun x y => ?_⟩
    induction x using OreLocalization.ind with | _ x s => ?_
    induction y using OreLocalization.ind with | _ y t => ?_
    rw [Subsingleton.elim x 0, Subsingleton.elim y 0, OreLocalization.zero_oreDiv,
      OreLocalization.zero_oreDiv]
  exact LinearEquiv.ofSubsingleton _ _

/-- Isomorphic modules in `T` have the same class in $\mathbb{G}(T)$. -/
@[category API, AMS 16 19]
theorem grothendieckClass_eq_of_linearEquiv {U V : Type v} [AddCommGroup U] [Module Λ U]
    [AddCommGroup V] [Module Λ V] (hU : MemT R Λ U) (hV : MemT R Λ V) (e : U ≃ₗ[Λ] V) :
    grothendieckClass R Λ U hU = grothendieckClass R Λ V hV := by
  refine (QuotientAddGroup.eq).mpr (AddSubgroup.subset_closure (Or.inl ?_))
  exact ⟨⟨ModuleCat.of Λ V, hV⟩, ⟨ModuleCat.of Λ U, hU⟩, ⟨e.symm⟩,
    by rw [neg_add_eq_sub]⟩

/-- The relation $[B] = [A] + [C]$ in $\mathbb{G}(T)$ for a short exact sequence
$0 \to A \to B \to C \to 0$ in `T`. -/
@[category API, AMS 16 19]
theorem grothendieckClass_eq_add_of_shortExact {A B C : Type v}
    [AddCommGroup A] [Module Λ A] [AddCommGroup B] [Module Λ B] [AddCommGroup C] [Module Λ C]
    (hA : MemT R Λ A) (hB : MemT R Λ B) (hC : MemT R Λ C)
    (f : A →ₗ[Λ] B) (g : B →ₗ[Λ] C)
    (hf : Function.Injective f) (hfg : Function.Exact f g) (hg : Function.Surjective g) :
    grothendieckClass R Λ B hB = grothendieckClass R Λ A hA + grothendieckClass R Λ C hC := by
  refine (QuotientAddGroup.eq).mpr ?_
  rw [neg_add_eq_sub, ← neg_sub]
  exact AddSubgroup.neg_mem _ (AddSubgroup.subset_closure (Or.inr ⟨⟨ModuleCat.of Λ A, hA⟩,
    ⟨ModuleCat.of Λ B, hB⟩, ⟨ModuleCat.of Λ C, hC⟩, ⟨f, g, hf, hfg, hg⟩, rfl⟩))

/--
**Conjecture (Roggenkamp, Kourovka 4.56 b).** Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring with
$1$ and $\Lambda$ an $R$-algebra which is finitely generated as an $R$-module. Let $T$ be the
class of `Λ`-modules $U$ admitting an exact sequence $0 \to P \to \Lambda^{(n)} \to U \to 0$
with $P_m \cong \Lambda_m^{(n)}$ for every maximal ideal $m$ of $R$, and let $\mathbb{G}(T)$
be the Grothendieck group of $T$ relative to short exact sequences.

If $\dim(\max(R)) = d < \infty$ and there are two epimorphisms
$\varphi \colon \Lambda^{(n)} \to U$, $\psi \colon \Lambda^{(n)} \to V$ with $n > d$ and
$[U] = [V]$ in $\mathbb{G}(T)$, then $\operatorname{Ker} \varphi \cong \operatorname{Ker} \psi$
as $\Lambda$-modules.

Here $\dim(\max(R))$ is the Krull dimension of the maximal spectrum of $R$ with the Zariski
topology, and $U, V \in T$ so that their classes in $\mathbb{G}(T)$ are defined.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 13 16 19]
theorem kourovka.«4.56».parts.b
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [Module.Finite R Λ]
    {d : ℕ} (hd : topologicalKrullDim (MaximalSpectrum R) = d)
    {U V : Type v} [AddCommGroup U] [Module Λ U] [AddCommGroup V] [Module Λ V]
    (hU : MemT R Λ U) (hV : MemT R Λ V)
    {n : ℕ} (hn : d < n)
    (φ : (Fin n → Λ) →ₗ[Λ] U) (ψ : (Fin n → Λ) →ₗ[Λ] V)
    (hφ : Function.Surjective φ) (hψ : Function.Surjective ψ)
    (hUV : grothendieckClass R Λ U hU = grothendieckClass R Λ V hV) :
    Nonempty (LinearMap.ker φ ≃ₗ[Λ] LinearMap.ker ψ) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.56»

items: `Ker φ = Ker ψ` is read as a Λ-module isomorphism `Nonempty (LinearMap.ker φ ≃ₗ[Λ] LinearMap.ker ψ)`, as prescribed by the decomposition notes (literal equality of submodules fails trivially).

`P_m ≅ Λ_m^{(n)}` is formalized as `IsLocallyFreeOfRankAt Λ m P n := Nonempty (P[S⁻¹] ≃ₗ[Λ[S⁻¹]] (Fin n → Λ[S⁻¹]))` where `S = Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid Λ m.asIdeal.primeCompl` is the (central) image of R∖m in Λ and `X[S⁻¹]` is Mathlib's `OreLocalization`. A bespoke `OreSet` instance for this central submonoid is provided (with proof). The Ore localization at a central multiplicative set is the usual localization Λ_m = R_m ⊗_R Λ, resp. P_m = R_m ⊗_R P, and the isomorphism is of Λ_m-modules as in the source.

In `MemT`, the module P of the exact sequence 0 → P → Λ^(n) → U → 0 is taken to be `LinearMap.ker φ` for the surjection φ; any such P is isomorphic to ker φ and local freeness is invariant under isomorphism, so this is equivalent to the literal existential over P.

`dim(max(R)) = d < ∞` is formalized as `topologicalKrullDim (MaximalSpectrum R) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)` with `d : ℕ` (Krull dimension of the maximal spectrum with the Zariski topology, not `ringKrullDim R`). This excludes the zero ring (whose maximal spectrum is empty, with dimension ⊥); for R = 0 the conjecture is trivially true anyway. `n > d` is `d < n` (strict).

The Grothendieck group is `FreeAbelianGroup (TObj R Λ) ⧸ grothendieckRelations R Λ`, where `TObj R Λ = {U : ModuleCat.{v} Λ // MemT R Λ U}` (modules in T living in the universe `v` of Λ; every module in T is a quotient of `Fin n → Λ`, hence isomorphic to one of these) and the relations are generated by `[A] - [B]` for Λ-isomorphic A, B in T and `[B] - ([A] + [C])` for short exact sequences 0 → A → B → C → 0 with all three terms in T (`Function.Injective f ∧ Function.Exact f g ∧ Function.Surjective g`). The iso relations are redundant (0 ∈ T) but included so the definition visibly matches 'free abelian group on isomorphism classes'.

U and V are quantified over `Type v` (the universe of Λ) so that their classes in `GrothendieckGroup R Λ` can be formed; this loses no generality since every module in T is isomorphic to a module in `Type v` and the statement is invariant under isomorphism.

`U ∈ T` and `V ∈ T` are taken as explicit hypotheses `hU hV : MemT R Λ U/V` (needed to form [U], [V]); no extra hypothesis that ker φ, ker ψ themselves are locally free of rank n is imposed (by Schanuel's lemma and cancellation over the semilocal rings Λ_m this follows automatically, but the source does not state it, so it is not assumed).
'Mod Λ' is left Λ-modules (`Module Λ U`); modules in T are automatically finitely generated, so no finiteness hypothesis on U, V is added.

Two `@[category API]` lemmas (`grothendieckClass_eq_of_linearEquiv`, `grothendieckClass_eq_add_of_shortExact`) test the bespoke Grothendieck group definition, as CONTRIBUTING.md asks for basic API tests of bespoke definitions.

The `OreSet` instance and the localization/Grothendieck-group definitions are generic and reusable; the repository convention would place them in `FormalConjecturesForMathlib/`, but the task restricts output to the single candidate file, so they live in the problem file.

reviewer_notes: Candidate verdicts. c01 is UNFAITHFUL: its `HasLocallyFreeKernel` requires e (mk (a • x)) = mk (a • ↑x) for all a, x; with a = 1 this forces the R_m-linear iso e to coincide with the localized inclusion P_m → (Λ^n)_m, so P_m ≅ Λ_m^n via e means U_m = 0 for every maximal m, i.e. T = {0} (U is finitely generated over R), and the conjecture becomes vacuous. c02 and c07 (tensor product P ⊗[R] R_m with a Λ-linear iso) are faithful: a Λ-linear map between modules on which R∖m acts invertibly is automatically R_m-linear, hence Λ_m-linear. c05 and c06 (LocalizedModule with an explicit Λ-intertwining condition on top of R_m-linearity) are faithful but verbose; c05 also quantifies the universe of T-objects freely, which is harmless (relations in the small T are relations in the full T, so the statement for the full T implies the small one). c03 and c04 are faithful Ore-localization formalizations equivalent to c08 (c03 uses d : WithBot ℕ∞ with d < ⊤, admitting the zero ring; c04 fixes universe Type and drops the redundant iso relation, which is derivable since 0 ∈ T). Interpretive choices common to all and mandated by the decomposition table: 'Ker φ = Ker ψ' read as Λ-module isomorphism (literal equality fails trivially); U, V implicitly in T; Mod Λ = left Λ-modules (finite generation is automatic for T); dim(max R) as the topological Krull dimension of MaximalSpectrum R — this excludes the zero ring (dimension ⊥), where the conjecture is trivially true anyway. The generic OreSet instance for `Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid Λ S` would ideally live in FormalConjecturesForMathlib; it is kept in the problem file because only one output file is permitted. Part a) was correctly dropped by all candidates (a request for a description, not a proposition).
